title: Mechanical energy loss
description: Essential: The response must correctly state the mechanical energy lost as mgL(1-cosθ).

title: Friction work expression
description: Essential: The response must correctly state the work done by friction as -mgL(1-cosθ).

title: Friction coefficient formula
description: Essential: The response must derive and state the kinetic friction coefficient as μ = mgL(1-cosθ)/(Fs).

title: Energy conservation reasoning
description: Important: The solution should apply energy conservation between the initial and final swing positions to find the energy loss.

title: Work-energy theorem application
description: Important: The solution must link the friction work to the mechanical energy loss via the work-energy theorem.

title: Work definition for friction
description: Important: The solution must correctly express the friction work as the product of friction force, sliding distance, and the cosine of the angle (which is -1).

title: Constant normal force assumption
description: Optional: The solution may note that the normal force F is given as constant, simplifying the work calculation.

title: Sign error in work
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the work done by friction is given with a positive sign, ignoring its dissipative nature.

title: Incorrect energy reference
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the potential energy change is miscalculated (e.g., using sinθ or incorrect height difference).
